title: Destructive htmx requests declare a confirmation

facts.note: Markup/template files where hx- attributes can appear; every hx-delete in them is in scope, new or pre-existing.

values: htmx_hypermedia_detector: hx-delete without hx-confirm/hx-prompt on the same opening tag
facts.note: Detector finding from the htmx_hypermedia_detector family on atdd.workspace.bun; scans every hx-delete occurrence, including untouched existing ones.

values: element with hx-delete added or modified
facts.note: Diff-level observer; only one trigger among several — existing unmodified violations are also in scope via the finding fact.
Task text mentions a destructive action in an htmx UI.

fires: A coder adds a button or link with hx-delete to a template and no hx-confirm/hx-prompt on that element.
An existing hx-delete element is edited and its hx-confirm is removed.
An existing, unmodified hx-delete element anywhere in the markup lacks hx-confirm/hx-prompt on its own opening tag (detector finds it regardless of the diff).
An hx-delete element relies on an hx-confirm placed on a neighbouring control or wrapper in the same file.
An hx-delete element lacks a same-element confirmation even though some other guard or handler exists elsewhere.
doesNotFire: An element with hx-post/hx-put/hx-patch only (governed by coder.htmx.verb-mutation-signals-progress).
An hx-delete element that carries hx-prompt instead of hx-confirm.
Non-markup files with no hx- attributes.

given: A markup element carrying `hx-delete` (newly added or already existing)
when: the markup is written, changed or checked
then: The same opening tag that carries `hx-delete` MUST also carry `hx-confirm="…"` (yes/no gate) or `hx-prompt="…"` (typed-input gate).
prefer: For high-value deletions use `hx-prompt` so the user types something meaningful rather than reflexively clicking OK (confirm vs prompt is a product decision on friction).
Express destructive requests with `hx-delete` so the guard is checkable.
avoid: Confirmation on a neighbouring control or elsewhere in the file — protects nothing.
A delete as `hx-post` to a `/…/delete` route, hiding the verb from this rule.
Suppressing, waiving or baselining the finding: this rule is `strict` (severity 2) — an unguarded delete is not suppressible; add the confirmation instead.
unless: An element carrying `hx-prompt` instead of `hx-confirm` satisfies the rule.
why: In hypermedia a delete is one attribute on a clickable element: no form submit, route transition or framework guard sits between click and request. htmx removes the handler where confirmation used to live, so it must be relocated onto the element as declarative `hx-confirm`, or it is lost in the migration.
evidence: htmx_hypermedia_detector reports no element whose opening tag carries `hx-delete` without `hx-confirm` or `hx-prompt`.
Reviewer confirms the confirmation attribute is co-located on the same element as `hx-delete`, not merely present in the file.
No suppression, waiver or baseline entry exists for this rule's findings (disposition strict).
verifier_detail: Detector is a zero-dependency Bun detector: find each `hx-delete`, extract the enclosing opening tag with a quote-aware scan, flag the element when that tag carries neither `hx-confirm` nor `hx-prompt`.
Check is CO-LOCATION on the same element, not mere presence of hx-confirm in the file; a confirmation on a neighbouring control protects nothing.
Destructive verb = `hx-delete` only; `hx-post`/`hx-put`/`hx-patch` are mutating but not inherently destructive and are governed by coder.htmx.verb-mutation-signals-progress.
Declared confirmation = `hx-confirm="…"` (yes/no gate) or `hx-prompt="…"` (typed-input gate); either satisfies.

Known blind spot (source exception): a delete implemented as `hx-post` to an explicit `/…/delete` route is not detected; that is a naming choice the rule cannot see, and it is why the verb should be `hx-delete`.
Rule identity metadata: disposition strict (applies policy.strict-disposition to this rule), severity 2: an unguarded delete is not suppressible.

Component-framework contrast (rationale context): there a destructive action passes through a handler and the confirmation lives in that handler where a reviewer sees it; `hx-confirm` is declarative precisely so it cannot be forgotten.
audit: schema_version 1.1.0; kind rule; status active; introduced_in 0.1.0.
Bun/htmx-stack realization of the agnostic "a destructive action requires explicit intent" obligation, enforced by the htmx_hypermedia_detector family implementation on atdd.workspace.bun.

sharedNodes.text: Generic strict disposition: a rule marked strict fails on every finding; no advisory mode, no ratchet baseline; its findings are not suppressible. Rules opt in via their own disposition metadata.
